subject.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle

question: Should resetSessionEntryLifecycle become the permanent public Plugin SDK contract for plugin-triggered session boundaries, or should the storage primitive remain internal behind a narrower scoped runtime operation?
rationale: Both designs can fix the Teams bug, but choosing what third-party plugins may call and which layer owns locked-harness release is a lasting API and compatibility decision that repository policy reserves for maintainers.

options.title: Approve the generic lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep the generic reset operation, make the scoped plugin runtime the canonical entry point, and land after the exact-head guard is green.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Keep the storage mutation primitive internal and expose only a smaller scoped runtime operation tailored to externally observed lifecycle boundaries.

options.title: Pause for redesign
options.body: Do not publish a lifecycle-reset API until another owner-approved core design establishes the permanent session-boundary contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Keep the generic reset operation, make the scoped plugin runtime the canonical entry point, and land after the exact-head guard is green.

likelyOwner.reason: He contributed the Teams lifecycle scope correction and is the documented product owner best positioned to approve a new public Plugin SDK contract.
